Gaps and implications

Your customer journey today: five steps, two of them capped

1

Your free training runs live once a week, on Wednesdays at 8pm ET, so the 95%* of your audience who aren't ready for your high-ticket offer yet can only start on one night.

2

One slot a week

Interest on a Thursday waits six days

A woman who finds you on a Thursday has to hold that interest until the next Wednesday at 8pm ET. Some will register and show up; many will have moved on by then.

Organic only

The training is only as full as this week's posting

Every seat depends on the reels and stories you post that week. When you post less, fewer women find the training, and the Academy pipeline thins with it.

Capped volume

Your fit check only sees who reaches Wednesday

The 3-question fit check is a good filter, but it can only qualify the women who get to it. More qualified women need more daily traffic, not more questions.

Your live training works. It's just limited to one night a week and to whoever saw your posts that week.

My recommendation

An always-on version of your training, fed by ads every day

Keep your live Wednesday training. Alongside it, an on-demand version of the class runs every day, fed by Meta ads. It sells your HLC Inauguration on the thank-you page and sends the women who are ready to an application on the replay page.

Removes the one-night limit

A woman who finds you can start the class the same day, whatever day it is, and every sign-up is an email you keep and can follow up with.

Turns the Inauguration into a natural next step

Right after she registers, she's at her most interested. That's when your $97 HLC Inauguration is offered, so the first purchase happens when she's warm, not cold.

The application on the replay page goes deeper than the 3 questions and filters for readiness before your team's calendar, and the pre-call emails warm her up for the Academy.

They watch a free class, many pick up the HLC Inauguration, and they join your email list. You get paid to start the relationship instead of losing them.

They watch to the end and apply on the replay page. The application shows you who they are, and the pre-call emails prepare them for the conversation about the Academy.

Here's what you'll learn

Five things we'll cover in 60 minutes

What a high-ticket sales conversation actually is

What happens on a real sales call, who is on it, and why the best ones feel like a conversation, not a pitch.

Script 1 · "Not pushy"

Hook (0 to 3s)

"If the word 'sales' makes you picture someone pushy, this is for you."

Body

"High-ticket sales done well is mostly listening. You ask good questions, you care about the answer, and you help someone decide. That's a skill, and it can be learned with practice."

CTA

"I'm teaching how it works in a free live masterclass, with a real role-play. Tap Sign up to save your seat."

Shot: talking to camera at night, city lights behind, on-screen text "not pushy" in rose gold.

Script 2 · "What's on the call"

Hook (0 to 3s)

"Here's what actually happens on a high-ticket sales call."

Body

"Someone has already shown interest. Your job is to understand what they want, show them whether the offer fits, and handle hesitation with calm, not pressure. Most people have never seen one done well."

CTA

"I'll walk you through one live in The Last Call Masterclass. It's free. Tap Sign up."

Shot: talking to camera, cut to a slide with the 4 call stages.

Script 3 · "I need to think about it"

Hook (0 to 3s)

"What do you say when someone says 'I need to think about it'?"

Body

"Most people either push or give up. There's a third way: get curious. Ask what they want to think through. It keeps the conversation honest and respectful, and it's one of the first things we practise."

CTA

"Want to hear it in a live role-play? Join my free masterclass. Tap Sign up below."

Shot: talking to camera, on-screen text of the question as she says it.
